speaker: den
text: You were snatching at them Saturday. I've a bag of balls here and the groundsman's left the shed light on, so do you want me to feed you a hundred?

speaker: den
text: You put three over the bar and you looked at the keeper before every one of them.

speaker: den
text: I've washed the kit here for thirty-one years and I've seen a lot of lads go through that. Most of them got out of it on a night like this.

speaker: den
text: You don't have to say owt. Stand on the D and I'll roll them in.

speaker: den
text: I do. And your boots will be clean on your peg by eight tomorrow, same as they always are.

speaker: den
text: Fair enough, you've trained all day. I'm out here most Thursdays if you change your mind.

speaker: den
text: Ten lots of ten, and I count them out loud so neither of us can cheat.

speaker: den
text: Do you want them from where you missed on Saturday, or from further out where it's harder?

speaker: den
text: Corners, then. Twenty yards is for when you can do the corners.

speaker: den
text: One more thing before we start. The gaffer's going to see that light from his office window. If he asks me in the morning, what am I telling him?

speaker: den
text: Ten.

speaker: den
text: Twenty.

speaker: den
text: That's thirty.

speaker: den
text: Forty, and keep your head down.

speaker: den
text: Fifty, so that's halfway.

speaker: den
text: Sixty.

speaker: den
text: Seventy, and stop looking at the goal.

speaker: den
text: Eighty.

speaker: den
text: Ninety.

speaker: den
text: And a hundred.

speaker: den
text: I'll be honest with you, I had you down for fifty.

speaker: den
text: It's dark, mind, and my feeding's not what it was. You were still looking up before you hit it.

speaker: den
text: I've a flask of soup in the van if you want a cup before you go. It's only tomato.

speaker: den
text: I've two more seasons in me. The wife says one. When I do go they'll give me a night, a dinner or a match or something, and I'd like you there. Lads always say yes and then they've signed for somebody in Spain.

speaker: den
text: See you tomorrow.

speaker: den
text: Thursday.

speaker: den
text: Then go and put them in the ice. We'll finish it another night.

speaker: den
text: I'll hold you to that.

speaker: den
text: That's all anybody can say.

speaker: gaffer
text: Was it you?

speaker: gaffer
text: Hm.

speaker: gaffer
text: What did he have you doing?

speaker: gaffer
text: On Saturday, when you get your chance, I want it low and I don't want to see you look up. Can you do that for me?

speaker: gaffer
text: Good lad.

speaker: gaffer
text: And next time, finish the hundred.

speaker: gaffer
text: Score like that and we'll talk about the penalties.

speaker: gaffer
text: Somebody had the shed light on till seven last night. Den says he can't think who.

speaker: gaffer
text: Next one's yours. Miss it and it goes back.

speaker: den
text: You were. I've had worse off better players, mind.

speaker: den
text: Go and stand on the D.

speaker: den
text: Aye, go on.

speaker: den
text: My grandson's started at the under-nines. He's a left back and he hates it, he wants to be you. I told him you'd been doing corners for a month and he said that sounded boring.

speaker: den
text: That's the most you've hit out here.

speaker: den
text: He'll be sick with nerves. I'll bring him.

speaker: den
text: Right.
